collections.title: OSINT Methodology Research | ALEX by RISE
collections.description: Browse research on open-source intelligence methods: collecting, validating and connecting public information, with original publication details and source links.
collections.intro: Open-source intelligence (OSINT) turns publicly available information into material that can support an investigation. The methodological questions matter as much as the tools: how information was found, whether it can be verified, and what conclusions the available evidence can support.
collections.scope: This collection contains papers assigned to ALEX’s OSINT Methodology research category. It brings together work on information collection, validation, linkage and the organisation of investigative work. It is a subject collection, rather than a list of papers selected for one particular kind of investigation.
collections.use: Use the bibliography to compare collection approaches, examine validation methods and trace the research behind an investigative technique. Consult the original paper for its data, assumptions and limitations before applying a method. A classification in this collection does not establish that a tool is suitable for a particular case.

collections.title: Phishing Analysis Research | ALEX by RISE
collections.description: Explore research classified for phishing analysis, including deceptive messages, URLs and websites, detection approaches and campaign evidence, with source links.
collections.intro: Phishing analysis examines deceptive messages, websites and supporting infrastructure to understand how an attempt works and how related activity might be recognised. Research can help investigators assess indicators and detection methods, while keeping the evidence behind a finding separate from a model’s prediction.
collections.scope: This bibliography contains papers assigned to ALEX’s Phishing Analysis investigation type. That assignment describes an investigative application; it is separate from the research category. Papers may therefore approach phishing through fraud research, machine learning, threat intelligence or other subjects represented in the accepted library.
collections.use: Use these references to investigate message and URL characteristics, compare detection approaches and find studies relevant to campaign analysis. Check the original study’s dataset, evaluation period and error rates: results from one dataset or period may not transfer to another investigation. These papers are research references, rather than a live feed of phishing indicators.
